faq_heading: Vancouver Heights real estate: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for Vancouver Heights. It has no local notes, street boundaries, schools or listing feed yet; see the open items below.

Vancouver Heights, Burnaby: 13 houses and 22 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September, with 5 and 1 sold in the month. It is one of 35 communities the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures break out for Burnaby.
Vancouver Heights homes listed and sold, June to September 2026

Vancouver Heights, September 2026. Detached houses: 13 listed at month end and 5 sold in September, a sales ratio of 38% (a sellers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 22 listed at month end and 1 sold in September, a sales ratio of 5% (a buyers’ market).

Condos and townhomes: 7 sold over 4 months against an average of 17.0 listed, about 9.7 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was July with 3 sold.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 16 in June to 13 in September (−18.8%), and it took 5.5% of the city’s 199 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 16 in June to 22 in September (+37.5%), and it took 0.9% of the city’s 750 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Vancouver Heights for detached houses in September (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in September (a buyers’ best bet).
Vancouver Heights share of Burnaby listings and sales by month

In Vancouver Heights, its share of the houses listed in Burnaby went from 3.4% in June to 2.8% in September and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 1.2% to 1.7%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

items.t: Vancouver Heights condos and townhomes for sale

blocks.text: Vancouver Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

19 houses sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $2,075,000 (the middle half sold between $1,665,000 and $2,221,500), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 11% sold above list. They had a median $770 per square foot, a median year built of 1978 and a median lot of 4,049 square feet. 15 condos sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $565,000 (the middle half sold between $491,500 and $976,900), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $790 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $397 a month.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 13 houses and 22 condos and townhomes listed in Vancouver Heights. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Vancouver Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 38% (a sellers’ market); condos and townhomes had 5% (a buyers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Vancouver Heights from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 11 houses and 7 condos and townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights over those 4 months; detached houses peaked in September with 5 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in July with 3 sold.

faq.q: How big is Vancouver Heights compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In September 2026, Vancouver Heights held 2.8% of the 458 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 1.7% of the 1,333 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses made up 37.1% of the 35 homes listed in Vancouver Heights and condos and townhomes made up 62.9%; of the 6 that sold, houses were 83.3% and condos and townhomes 16.7%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Vancouver Heights than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 16 in June to 13 in September 2026 (−18.8%); condos and townhomes rose from 16 in June to 22 in September 2026 (+37.5%).

faq.q: What did houses in Vancouver Heights sell for?
faq.a: 19 houses sold in Vancouver Heights between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,075,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Vancouver Heights?
faq.a: The median was 21 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (11% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
